function: Learned hybrid beamforming (precoder and combiner) by deep-unfolded manifold optimization (DU-HBFN), plus Res-DnCNN denoising of the tracked channel; channel tracking itself is model-driven (pp. 8-10).
system: Aircraft and ground-BS UPAs, K_A/K_B 8/8 to 24/24 antennas, fully connected hybrid, 2 RF chains each, 16 subcarriers; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 11, 13).
method: Deep unfolding of iterative manifold-optimization HBF with trainable step sizes, unsupervised MSE loss, layer-by-layer offline training; Res-DnCNN denoiser trained on NMSE (supervised); Adam (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Own simulated A2G geometric MIMO-OFDM channel (1 LoS + 4 NLoS, Rician factor, uniform AoA/AoD, delay U[0,16Ts], CN(0,1) gains), generated offline; no standard model or measurements (pp. 3, 11).
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for training and testing (10/1/1 batches of 128 train/val/test); tests sweep SNR, antenna size K_A/K_B, CSI error NMSE 0.08; no unseen scenario stated (pp. 11, 13-14).
baselines: Non-learned: fully-digital MMSE (FD), iterative manifold-optimization I-HBF, LMMSE channel estimation; learned: CNN-HBF [20] with MSE loss; own-variant CD-I-HBF (Res-DnCNN + I-HBF) (pp. 12-14).
metrics: NMSE of tracked channel (vs SNR, pilots); hybrid-beamforming MSE (vs SNR, antenna size); training loss vs epoch (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Closed-form order 2XOP(4K^2Ns+7KNs^2+3KNs+2Ns^3+2ONs^3) operations for DU-HBFN, lower than I-HBF; 2OP trainable parameters; no runtime reported (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "We adopt a geometric channel model with one LoS path and L NLoS paths"; p. 11: "the simulated channel realizations are utilized for the offline training". Custom A2G simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "The data set consists of the training set, the validation set, and the test set"; p. 13: "MSE versus antenna configuration with SNR = {4, 6, 10} dB". Antenna-size and CSI-error sweeps only; the paper never states a train/test mismatch, transfer or retraining.
q3_support: p. 12: "a convolutional neural network (CNN) was utilized to design the HBF"; p. 13: "the MSE achieved by the CNN-HBF is much larger than that achieved by the DU-HBFN"; p. 13: "significantly outperforms I-HBF(5, 2)".
q4_support: p. 9: "We now analyze the computational complexity of the DU-HBFN" (formula follows); p. 10: "the parameter dimension of the DU-HBFN is 2OP".
q5_support: p. 11: "the simulated channel realizations are utilized for the offline training". Data come from the paper's own model; no code or data link is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: PDF is the published TCOM paper; title and DOI match on p. 1. Area 6 chosen because the learned HBF serves an aeronautical air-to-ground link (aircraft at 8000 m, p. 11); if the reviewer does not count this link as NTN, the area is 3. Channel tracking (polynomial regression, quaternion, LS) is not learned. Table I (p. 11) gives no carrier frequency or antenna counts; K_A/K_B come from Figs. 10(b) and 11(b). q2 borderline: p. 14 says the cascaded networks "can flexibly achieve the robust A2G beamforming under different antenna configurations", but the antenna configuration used for training is never stated, so no train/test mismatch is explicit; reviewer to confirm.
